paper.title: Phased Exploration with Greedy Exploitation in Stochastic Combinatorial Partial Monitoring Games

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic combinatorial partial monitoring (CPM) game with linear feedback
unmapped: Adversary outcomes theta(t) i.i.d. from unknown distribution p on [0,1]^n; feedback is M_x theta(t) for known matrices M_x
Expected reward depends only on (x, mean theta*_p) (Assumption 1), Lipschitz in theta with constant R (Assumption 3)
Existence of a global observable set sigma with M_sigma of full column rank (Assumption 2)
Learner's action set may be exponentially large or even infinite; access via argmax oracle
Learner knows reward function, matrices M_x and the global observable set
settings.definition_quote: The adversary fixes a distribution $p$ on $[0,1]^n$ before start of the game ... On playing action $x(t)$, the learner receives a feedback $M_{x(t)} \cdot \theta(t) \in \mathbb{R}^{m_x}$. ... R(T)= T \cdot \max_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \E [r(x,\theta)] - \sum_{t=1}^T \E [r(x(t), \theta(t))]

unmapped: Adversary outcomes i.i.d. on [0,1]^n with linear feedback M_x theta
Assumptions 1-3 (mean-dependent reward, global observable set, Lipschitz expected reward)
Algorithm uses argmax and arg-secondmax oracles, and knows R, beta_sigma, R_max
settings.definition_quote: Consider Algorithm~\ref{alg:combined} run with knowledge of the number $T$ of rounds.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic CPM game with unique optimal action (Assumption 4), known horizon
unmapped: Adversary outcomes i.i.d. on [0,1]^n with linear feedback M_x theta
Algorithm uses argmax and arg-secondmax oracles
settings.definition_quote: {\bf Assumption 4. (Unique Optimal Action)} The optimal action $x^* = \argmax_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \bar{r}(x, \theta^*_p)$ is unique.

algorithms.name: PEGE (Phased Exploration with Greedy Exploitation) framework for CPM

bound.expression_latex: R_{max} |\sigma| T^{2/3} + 2 R \beta_{\sigma} T^{2/3} \sqrt{ \log 2e^2  + 2 \log T}  + R_{max}

symbols.R_max: maximum expected reward over actions and outcomes
symbols.sigma_size: size |sigma| of the global observable set
symbols.beta_sigma: constant depending on transformation matrices of the global observable set (Eq. global-bound)

source.label: thm:distributionindependentregret
source.quote: When Algorithm~\ref{alg:PhaseForced} is initialized with the parameters $C(a)= \log a$, $\alpha=1/2$ and $\beta=0$, and the online game is played over $T$ rounds, we get the following bound on expected regret: R(T) \le R_{max} |\sigma| T^{2/3} + 2 R \beta_{\sigma} T^{2/3} \sqrt{ \log 2e^2  + 2 \log T}  + R_{max}

results.notes: Paper's R (Lipschitz constant) mapped to L_lip. Regret defined via expected reward function of mean, i.e., pseudo-regret. Algorithm does not take T as input (delta = 1/(KT) only in analysis), so marked anytime; proof uses approximation K ~ T^{1/(1+alpha)} for large K.

symbols.sum_Delta_sigma: sum of gaps Delta_x over actions x in the global observable set sigma
symbols.h: tuning parameter h > 0 of the exploitation length
symbols.beta_sigma: constant depending on matrices of the global observable set

source.label: thm:distributiondependentregret1
source.quote: When Algorithm~\ref{alg:PhaseForced} is initialized with the parameters $C(a)= h \cdot a$, for a tuning parameter $h>0$, $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=1$, and the online game is played over $T$ rounds, we get the following bound on expected regret: R(T) \le \sum_{x \in \sigma} \Delta_x \left(\dfrac{\log T}{h} \right)^2 + ...

results.notes: Paper's Delta is the minimum positive gap -> Delta_min; R -> L_lip.

symbols.sum_Delta_sigma: sum of gaps Delta_x over actions x in the global observable set sigma
symbols.beta_sigma: constant depending on matrices of the global observable set

tuning: C(a) = h*a with 0 < h < Delta^2/(4 R^2 beta_sigma^2)

source.label: thm:distributiondependentregret2
source.quote: When Algorithm~\ref{alg:PhaseForced} is initialized with the parameters $C(a)= h \cdot a$, for a tuning parameter $0<h< \frac{\Delta^2}{4 R^2 \beta^2_{\sigma}}$, $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=0$, and the online game is played over $T$ rounds, we get the following bound on expected regret: R(T) \le \sum_{x \in \sigma} \Delta_x \dfrac{\log T}{h} + \dfrac{2 e^2 \Delta_{max}}{\frac{\Delta^2}{4 R^2 \beta^2_{\sigma}} - h}

results.notes: Valid tuning of h requires gap knowledge (h below Delta^2/(4R^2 beta^2)); in appendix, used inside PEGE2.

symbols.beta_sigma: constant depending on matrices of the global observable set

tuning: w(b) = sqrt(R^2 beta_sigma^2 log(4 e^2 b^2/delta)/b)

source.label: thm:gap
source.quote: Suppose Assumption 4 holds and $T_1(\delta) < T_0$. Then with probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:gap} stops in $T_1(\delta)$ episodes and outputs an estimate $\hat{\Delta}$ that satisfies $\frac{1}{2} \Delta \le \hat{\Delta} \le \frac{3}{2} \Delta$.

results.notes: Bound on number of episodes (each of |sigma| rounds) to estimate the gap within factor [1/2,3/2] w.p. 1-delta. Claims 2 and 3 (threshold behaviour) not recorded separately.

bound.expression_latex: B_1(T) = 2(2 R \beta_\sigma |\sigma|^2 R^2_{max} T)^{2/3} \sqrt{\log (4e^2 T^3}) + R_{max}

symbols.beta_sigma: constant depending on matrices of the global observable set

source.label: thm:combined
source.quote: If Assumption 4 fails, then the expected regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:combined} is bounded as $R(T) \le B_1(T)$

results.notes: Holds only when the optimal action is not unique.

bound.expression_latex: \frac{256 R^2 \beta_\sigma^2}{\Delta^2} \log \frac{512 e^2 R^2 \beta_\sigma^2 T}{\Delta^2} R_{max} |\sigma| + \sum_{x \in \sigma} \Delta_x \frac{36 R^2 \beta_\sigma^2 \log T}{\Delta^2} + \frac{8 e^2 R^2 \beta_\sigma^2}{\Delta^2} + R_{max}

symbols.beta_sigma: constant depending on matrices of the global observable set
symbols.sum_Delta_sigma: sum of gaps over actions in sigma

source.label: thm:combined
source.quote: If Assumption 4 holds, then the expected regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:combined} is bounded as R(T) \le B_2(T) if T_1(\delta) < T_0

results.notes: Delta is gap between optimal and second best action.

source.label: thm:combined
source.quote: R(T) \le ... O(T^{2/3} \log T) & \text{ if } \ T_0 \le T_1(\delta)
